result: I’d want to cultivate empathy in every corner of the world. Not just a polite, surface-level kind of consideration, but a deep, genuine practice of stepping into another person’s emotions, perspectives, and challenges. If empathy became the default lens through which we viewed each other—across borders, backgrounds, beliefs—it could fundamentally shift how we address injustice, inequality, and suffering. We’d likely see more compassion in policymaking, more kindness in everyday interactions, and ultimately more collective resolve to solve global problems with unity rather than division. It wouldn’t be a quick fix for all the world’s troubles, but it would create a common ground where people truly listen and care about what others are going through. That single shift, I believe, could unlock countless positive changes that ripple out far beyond the individual.
